description:
A gate that is not required for an issue is reported three ways: a typed `GateNotRequiredError`, an `anyhow!` and a `bail!`. Only the typed error maps to the invalid-argument exit code.

## Background

- `GateNotRequiredError` (`crates/jit/src/commands/gate.rs:37-43`) is raised by `pass_gate` (`gate.rs:823`) and by manual evaluation (`commands/mod.rs:1613`).
- `fail_gate` raises `anyhow!` (`gate.rs:1039-1043`).
- `required_automated_gate` raises `bail!` (`commands/gate_check.rs:204-209`; callers `:776,896,959`).
- Typed matching lives in `main.rs:79` (`error_to_error_code` maps it to `InvalidArgument`), `main.rs:719-730` (JSON details `issue_id`, `key`) and `main.rs:9063`.
- No consumer matches the message text, and tests check exit codes (`tests/cli_gate/gate_evaluate_exit_code_test.rs:205,237`).

`gate fail` (`main.rs:5312`) is the user-visible change: a non-required gate there exits through the invalid-argument code instead of the generic gate-error fallback.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Every command path that finds a gate not required for an issue returns `GateNotRequiredError`.
- [hard] REQ-02: No `anyhow!` or `bail!` reports that condition in `commands/gate.rs` or `commands/gate_check.rs`.
- [hard] REQ-03: Failing a gate that is not required exits with the invalid-argument code, proven by one CLI test.

## Notes

The `main.rs` classifier already maps the typed error and needs no change.
title: Report a non-required gate through one typed error
